title: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry: Chapter Introduction
subject: Chemistry
objective: One drop of water holds about 1.7 × 10²¹ molecules. The chapter shows how chemists measure matter and count its particles with the mole.

fill.q: A pure substance made of only one kind of atom is an ____.
Lavoisier showed that in a chemical reaction mass is neither created nor ____.
Working out the amounts of reactants and products from a balanced equation is called ____.
Dalton said that all matter is made of ____.

tf.explain: Air is a mixture: its gases keep their own properties and their proportion can vary.
Hydrogen and oxygen are combined in a fixed ratio.

tf.q: In a chemical reaction the total mass of the products equals the total mass of the reactants.
tf.explain: This is the law of conservation of mass.

tf.q: One mole of every substance has the same mass.
tf.explain: One mole always has the same number of particles, but molar masses differ.

ar.a: The mole is a counting unit.
ar.r: One mole always means 6.022 × 10²³ entities, just as one dozen means 12.
ar.explain: R explains why the mole counts particles.

ar.a: Burning paper appears to lose mass.
ar.r: Mass is destroyed when a substance burns.
ar.explain: A is true because the gases formed escape; R is false: mass is conserved.

mcq.q: Which of these is a mixture?
mcq.explain: Air is a mixture of gases.

mcq.q: In 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, how many moles of O₂ react with 4 mol of H₂?
mcq.explain: H₂ : O₂ = 2 : 1, so 4 mol H₂ needs 2 mol O₂.

mcq.q: Who proposed the atomic theory in 1808?
mcq.explain: John Dalton, building on the laws of chemical combination.

num.q: How many molecules are in one drop of water (0.05 g, molar mass 18 g mol⁻¹)?
In 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, how many moles of water form from 4 mol of H₂?
Find the molar mass of water (H = 1, O = 16).

short.q: What is the chapter Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry about?
short.solution: Matter and its kinds, measurement (SI units, significant figures), the laws of chemical combination that led to Dalton's atoms, the mole concept and stoichiometry: chemistry as counting particles.

short.q: Why do chemists need the mole?
short.solution: Atoms are too small and too many to count one by one, so they are counted in groups of 6.022 × 10²³, just as eggs are counted in dozens.

match.explain: Elements have one kind of atom, compounds a fixed combination, mixtures any proportion; a mole is a fixed number of particles.
